record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Develop a Fundamental Theorem for PEPS in two and higher dimensions that applies to the largest possible class of projected entangled pair states, interpolating between the currently understood normal case and the fully general case where equality is undecidable.

evidence.quote: Question 11 Give a Fundamental Theorem in 2D (and higher dimensions) for the largest possible family of PEPS.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on a two-dimensional lattice is defined by associating to each site a tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times D \times D \times D \times D}$ with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of bond dimension $D$, and contracting copies of $A$ along the edges of a finite region $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ (with chosen boundary conditions) to obtain a vector $|\Psi_\Lambda(A)\rangle$ in the physical Hilbert space $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes |\Lambda|}$.

A "Fundamental Theorem" for a class $\mathcal{C}$ of PEPS tensors is a theorem of the following form: there exists an explicit list of local "gauge" relations on tensors (such as application of invertible matrices on virtual indices, possibly together with additional structural moves) such that, for every pair $A, B \in \mathcal{C}$, one has $|\Psi_\Lambda(A)\rangle = |\Psi_\Lambda(B)\rangle$ for all sufficiently large regions $\Lambda$ if and only if $A$ and $B$ are related by a finite sequence of these gauge relations.

For one-dimensional Matrix Product States, such a fundamental theorem is known in full generality. In two dimensions, it is established for the subclass of "normal" PEPS (tensors whose associated transfer-type map becomes injective after blocking). At the other extreme, equality of PEPS for arbitrary tensors is known to be undecidable, ruling out any complete fundamental theorem for the full class.

Problem: Identify a class $\mathcal{C}$ of two-dimensional (and, more generally, $d$-dimensional with $d \ge 2$) PEPS tensors that strictly contains the normal PEPS but is as large as possible while still admitting an explicit Fundamental Theorem in the above sense, and prove the corresponding theorem for $\mathcal{C}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. While a Fundamental Theorem is established for normal PEPS in 2D and undecidability results (e.g., Phys. Rev. Lett. 125, 210504) preclude a fully general version, recent surveys and works (such as the 2020 review on MPS/PEPS concepts, symmetries, and theorems, and 2024–2025 works on PEPS with flexible geometry and injective PEPS complexity) continue to identify the extension of the Fundamental Theorem to broader-than-normal classes of 2D PEPS as an outstanding goal, with no complete resolution found.

status_evidence.title: Matrix Product States and Projected Entangled Pair States: Concepts, Symmetries, and Theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Extending the Fundamental Theorem in 2D beyond normal tensors becomes a crucial question to solve... fill the gap between the restricted case of normal tensors and the undecidable general case.
status_evidence.claim: The extension of the Fundamental Theorem to broader classes of 2D PEPS is identified as an open and crucial question.

status_evidence.title: Projected Entangled Pair States: Fundamental Analytical and Numerical Limitations
status_evidence.snippet: It is impossible to fully characterize all the ways in which symmetries can be realized in PEPS... the question whether a PEPS has a certain symmetry is undecidable.
status_evidence.claim: A fully general fundamental theorem cannot exist due to undecidability, motivating the search for the largest decidable subclass.
